    assert run([("PUSH", 3), ("NEG",)]) == [-3]

        run([("PUSH", 1), ("PUSH", 0), ("MOD",)])

content.text: I changed one line in `solution/core.py`, and the visible suite now passes (3 passed). The cause was the operand order in the shared handler for the binary operators (ADD, SUB, MUL, DIV, MOD, EQ, LT, GT). It ran `a, b = pop(), pop()`, which puts the top of the stack in `a`, so the right-hand operand was treated as the left one. That one mistake caused all three failures: `1 2 LT` was evaluated as `2 < 1`, `1 0 DIV` checked the wrong operand for zero so `VMZeroDivision` was never raised, and `x 1 SUB` computed `1 - x`, so the countdown never reached zero and hit the step limit. The fix pops the top of the stack into `b` and the item below it into `a` (`b, a = pop(), pop()`), the same pattern `SWAP` already uses. I left the rest of the code alone; one thing I noticed but didn't change is that `jump_to` accepts a target equal to the program length, which just ends the run.
